**Lower bound.** Every round, all 40 players play (20 courts, 2 players each). A player therefore plays one match per round and needs 39 distinct opponents, so the tournament lasts at least 39 rounds.

**Achievability.** I could not verify that 39 rounds is achievable for 20 courts. I checked small cases by hand: 2 courts (4 players) finish in 3 = 2n−1 rounds, and 3 courts (6 players) finish in 5 = 2n−1 rounds. For 4 courts I tried several branches and each hit a dead end, though that search was not exhaustive. There is also a parity constraint: with an even number of courts, each round exactly two players change parity class (the court-1 loser and the court-20 winner), which constrains which pairs can meet when. I did not resolve whether this forces extra rounds for 20 courts.

So the answer is 39 only if a 39-round schedule exists for 20 courts. I believe it does, based on the small cases and on the counting slack, but I have not constructed or verified one.

ANSWER: 39
